raw_response:
I farm only 2 mu, so I count every bag, but I still do not like to cut fertilizer too hard. If wheat or maize loses yield, that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on inputs. I have done wheat-maize for many years, and I will stay with that. Around Quzhou, if water is available from the well, wheat cannot be left thirsty at jointing and grain filling, and maize cannot be left short of water around big flare and filling. I do not chase fancy new methods every year. I do what has worked here, then adjust a little. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed from the usual dealer, because old seed does not compete well now. For wheat, I will put a heavier base fertilizer and then topdress nitrogen once when the crop stands up and starts growing hard in spring. For maize, I will put part of the fertilizer at planting and the rest before the big growth period, because if maize runs short then, the ears stay small. On 2 mu, family labor is enough, so I will manage it carefully, spray when I see disease, worms, or heavy grass, and keep the field clean. Yield is what pays the year, so I will spend enough to keep both crops safe.
